meta.scope: Taiwan Batch 10 — Cross-Strait / Chinese connections deep pass. Expands the existing ECFA and MAC nodes with early-harvest execution statistics, detailed investment geography and flow decline, people-exchange series, and an explicit cross-strait meta-node that can sit in productive tension with the US–Taiwan economic-security and semiconductor-sovereignty clusters. Explicit referenced_by lists for force-layout edge strength.
meta.strategy_note: User request to formalise the Chinese connections. These nodes quantify both the residual commercial interdependence and the sharp relative decoupling (trade share and especially investment share). They form the natural opposing pole to the ART / investment-MOU / export-control architecture.

candidates.title: Cross-Strait Economic Statistics Monthly / MAC compilation
candidates.description: Regular official compilation of cross-strait trade, investment and people-exchange indicators. Draws on Customs, Investment Commission, immigration and tourism sources to present a coherent Taiwan-side picture of the economic relationship. Primary statistical product for cross-strait analysis.
referenced_by: Customs trade statistics (China / Hong Kong partner share)
Outbound investment analysis and BOP financial account
candidates.notes: Institutional core of the cross-strait statistical cluster. Already flagged in earlier batches; this node formalises it as the central recurring series.

candidates.title: ECFA Early Harvest List execution statistics (goods and services)
candidates.publisher: Ministry of Economic Affairs / International Trade Administration / ECFA-related offices
candidates.description: Official statistics on the implementation of the ECFA Early Harvest programmes for goods (tariff reductions, certificates of origin issued, estimated tariff savings) and the limited services openings. Early-harvest share of Taiwan’s exports to China has declined markedly over the past decade.
referenced_by: ECFA legal text and subsequent policy evaluations
Customs trade data and tariff-revenue analysis
candidates.notes: Quantifies the preferential layer of the relationship. The declining relative importance of the early-harvest list is itself a structural signal of decoupling.

candidates.title: Cross-Strait Economic Cooperation Framework Agreement (ECFA) — legal instrument
candidates.publisher: Republic of China (Taiwan) / People’s Republic of China
candidates.description: Framework agreement signed in 2010 that established the Early Harvest programmes and the institutional architecture for subsequent cross-strait economic negotiations. Continuously cited as the principal preferential trade instrument across the Strait.
referenced_by: Subsequent (largely stalled) goods and services negotiation records
candidates.notes: Foundational recurring-citation node. Already present in earlier batches; reinforced here with clearer links to the execution statistics.

candidates.title: Taiwan outbound investment to Mainland China — flow and stock statistics
candidates.publisher: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs
candidates.description: Approved cases and amounts of Taiwanese investment in Mainland China. Cumulative stock since 1991 exceeds US$210 billion and historically dominated Taiwan’s outbound investment; annual flows have fallen to low single-digit shares of total outbound investment in recent years (3.8 % in 2025, lower still in early 2026).
referenced_by: BOP financial account and international investment position
candidates.notes: Highest-visibility investment node. The collapse in relative share is one of the clearest quantitative markers of structural decoupling.

candidates.title: Geographic distribution of Taiwanese investment in Mainland China
candidates.description: Breakdown of approved investment by Mainland province / municipality. Jiangsu, Shanghai, Guangdong and Fujian have consistently absorbed the large majority of the stock and of residual flows.
referenced_by: Outbound investment to Mainland China statistics
candidates.notes: Spatial detail that links the investment stock to specific Mainland industrial regions.

candidates.title: Mainland Chinese investment in Taiwan — approved cases and amounts
candidates.publisher: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs
candidates.description: Statistics on approved inbound investment from Mainland China. Volumes remain tightly restricted and numerically small relative to Taiwan’s overall FDI inflows and to the historical outbound stock.
candidates.notes: Asymmetric counterpart to the large outbound stock. Highlights the controlled and limited nature of capital inflows from the Mainland.

candidates.title: Cross-strait trade share of Taiwan’s total trade (exports and imports)
candidates.description: Time-series indicators of the share of Taiwan’s total exports and total trade accounted for by Mainland China (and China + Hong Kong). Documents the decline from peak dependence (exports to China+HK ~44 % in 2020) to substantially lower shares by 2025.
referenced_by: Headline trade statistics and BOP goods account
candidates.notes: Key dependence / decoupling indicator. Provides the quantitative backbone for arguments about structural change in the commercial relationship.

candidates.title: Cross-strait people-exchange and visitor statistics
candidates.publisher: Mainland Affairs Council / National Immigration Agency / Tourism Administration / Ministry of Education
candidates.description: Statistics on outbound travel by Taiwan residents to Mainland China, inbound visitors from the Mainland, and student / youth exchange numbers. Series are highly sensitive to political and public-health conditions and have been the subject of recent official concern regarding asymmetric youth exchanges.
candidates.notes: People-to-people layer of the relationship. Complements the purely commercial trade and investment nodes.

candidates.title: Cross-strait financial and banking linkages (where statistically tracked)
candidates.publisher: Financial Supervisory Commission / Central Bank / MAC-related sources
candidates.description: Available official statistics and regulatory reporting on Taiwanese banks’ presence in Mainland China, residual financial linkages, and related prudential indicators. Limited relative to the historical trade and investment stock.
referenced_by: Outbound investment and corporate exposure analysis
candidates.notes: Financial-channel counterpart to the trade and direct-investment nodes. Relatively constrained by regulation.

candidates.title: Cross-Strait / Chinese-connections architecture (meta-node)
candidates.publisher: Derived from MAC, Investment Commission, ECFA offices, Customs and related sources
candidates.description: Meta-node that binds ECFA (legal + early-harvest execution), MAC Cross-Strait Economic Statistics, outbound and inbound investment series, trade-share indicators, people-exchange statistics and residual financial linkages into a coherent cross-strait cluster. Explicitly positioned as the commercial and historical counterpart (and partial opposite) to the US–Taiwan economic-security and semiconductor-sovereignty architecture.
referenced_by: All detailed cross-strait nodes in this batch
US–Taiwan ART / investment MOU / export-control nodes (Batch 8)
Semiconductor supply-chain and trade statistics that still contain Mainland intermediate-goods flows
National accounts, BOP and economic-security assessments
candidates.notes: Integrating node designed so the force layout can treat ‘Chinese commercial connections’ as a high-mass object that pulls against the chips–sovereignty and US economic-security clusters. Captures both residual interdependence and the measured decoupling.
